title: Introduce staggered dedicated scale policy and utilization telemetry bridge
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a staggered scaling policy for Dedicated fleets to reduce mass simultaneous resizes and introduces a telemetry bridge that emits per-tenant utilization deltas to the console and billing pipelines. No API surface breaking changes.
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleet scale events often cluster (hourly rollups, cron jobs, warm-pool fills), causing short-lived oscillations in cluster utilization and increased tail latency for other tenants. This PR implements a staggered scale policy (stagger windows + concurrency fences) that spaces reservation/resizing operations across configurable windows and emits a new utilization-telemetry bridge so operators can correlate scale events with observed per-tenant SLO impact.

What this change does: 1) New policy: autoscaler/policy/staggered.go implements a windowed scheduler that groups tenant scale intents and releases them across sub-windows to reduce peak allocation churn. It includes a concurrency_fence that prevents more than N concurrent resizes per pool. 2) Controller integration: pkg/autoscaler/controller.go wires the policy into the reconcile loop, adds backoff jitter to avoid synchronized retries, and exposes knobs in the Dedicated CRD. 3) Telemetry bridge: internal/telemetry/util_bridge.go (and a lightweight shim in observability-pack/) aggregates per-tenant util deltas, computes p50/p90/p99 change rates, and emits both metrics and structured events to the console for downstream billing and incident tooling. 4) Docs and Helm: docs/dedicated/autoscaling.md and helm/redwood-dedicated/values.yaml add configuration docs and sane defaults.

Commits: - 1f3c9a2 add staggered policy and unit tests - 4b2e1b7 integrate policy with controller and CRD knobs - 9d7f0c5 telemetry bridge and metrics adapters - a0f4e21 docs and helm defaults - fixup: respond to review comments (nits, additional tests)

Files changed (high level): - pkg/autoscaler/controller.go (logic to schedule staggered operations, backoff) - pkg/apis/dedicated/v1alpha1/types.go (new policy config fields) - autoscaler/policy/staggered.go (core algorithm + tests) - internal/telemetry/util_bridge.go (aggregation + emitter) - observability-pack/bridges/README.md (usage) - helm/redwood-dedicated/values.yaml (defaults) - docs/dedicated/autoscaling.md - pkg/autoscaler/simulator/staggered_sim_test.go - e2e/dedicated/staggered_scaling.yaml (demo)

Testing and CI: Unit tests added for scheduler edge cases (concurrent tenants, clock drift, partial failures). A small simulator validates that stagger windows reduce simultaneity under synthetic load. CI: linux/amd64 unit tests and integration job passed; e2e pipeline rerun (flaky network test fixed). CI status: pass.

Review discussion summary: - Owen: requested clearer failure semantics for partial resize failures; I added a rollback-on-failure mode and a retry window with exponential backoff. - Priya: asked for observability hooks — added structured events with tenant_id and intent_id so the console can link UI events to scale ops. Also added p90 latency change metric. - Diego: questioned default window sizing; we tuned defaults to conservative values (60s window with 6 sub-steps) and added a helm value for operators.

Open design tradeoffs discussed: - Aggressive grouping reduces API churn but increases tail risk for tenants that need immediate capacity; introduced opt-out per-tenant and emergency bypass to support SLA-critical customers. - The telemetry bridge intentionally samples high-cardinality attributes at 1% by default to limit backend costs; operators can tune sampling via helm.

Migration and rollout plan: Default-off in main for two weeks (feature gate: StaggeredDedicatedScaler). After internal dogfood in staging and observing console telemetry for regressions, we will flip the gate for non-enterprise tiers and monitor p50/p95 latency and allocation churn graphs. Release note: staggered scaling policy (opt-in) and telemetry bridge added.

Merge outcome: PR merged via squash-and-merge after one approving review and CI green. Changelog entry prepared and documentation updated.
notes: Should monitor tenant emergency bypass usage
Consider auto-tuning sub-window size based on cluster occupancy in a follow-up
